Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the StellarTech Semiconductor Q1 2024 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today's call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Alicia Johnson, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alicia Johnson, VP of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and welcome to StellarTech Semiconductor’s Q1 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Dr. Evelyn Reed, CEO; Mr. Robert Chen, CFO; and Dr. Jian Li, Chief Technology Officer.
Earlier today, we published our earnings press release and slides, which are available on our IR site. Please note this call may contain forward-looking statements. Now, I’ll turn it over to Dr. Reed.

Dr. Evelyn Reed, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Alicia. Hello, everyone.

Let’s start with a look at the quarter:

This quarter, we achieved significant progress, including a healthy 3% increase in wafer ASPs, driven by a favorable product mix shift towards advanced nodes within our 12-inch wafer production. We remain committed to investing in technology leadership, expanding our value-added services, and diversifying our geographic footprint to sustain and grow our ASPs in the long term. While we are mindful of the ongoing macroeconomic uncertainties, we are confident in our ability to navigate the challenges and deliver strong financial results.

We’re seeing a decrease in consolidated DOI from 92 days in Q2 2023 to 86 days in Q3 2023. This 6-day reduction represents a significant improvement and puts us closer to our target DOI of 80 days by the end of fiscal year 2024. This improvement in DOI translated to an increase in inventory turnover from 3.9 times per year in Q2 to 4.2 times per year in Q3.

These results reflect our strategy in action. I’ll now hand it over to Mr. Chen to discuss the financials.

Mr. Robert Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Dr. Reed, and hello, everyone.

Let’s take a closer look at the numbers:

As Dr. Reed mentioned, we saw a decrease in consolidated DOI from 92 days in Q2 2023 to 86 days in Q3 2023. This 6-day reduction represents a significant improvement and puts us closer to our target DOI of 80 days by the end of fiscal year 2024. This improvement in DOI translated to an increase in inventory turnover from 3.9 times per year in Q2 to 4.2 times per year in Q3. The total value of inventory on hand at the end of Q3 was $3.1 billion, down from $3.3 billion at the end of Q2. This reduction reflects both decreased carrying costs and a more efficient flow of goods through our supply chain. In Mobile Communication & Computing, DOI decreased from 78 days in Q2 to 68 days in Q3, largely driven by robust demand for our new "Aether" smartphone line, which experienced a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion. We also implemented a \"demand sensing\" initiative that leverages AI to better predict consumer demand and optimize production schedules, reducing excess inventory of older models. We also saw benefits from strategically reducing the number of components held in inventory and leveraging better supplier relationships to decrease lead times. In Automotive, DOI remains elevated at 105 days, a slight improvement from 108 days in Q2. The ongoing semiconductor shortage continues to disrupt production schedules, leading to a build-up of partially completed vehicles and components. We are actively working with our suppliers to secure chip allocation and are exploring alternative component sourcing options to mitigate the impact of the shortage. In the consumer segment, DOI remained relatively flat at 95 days in Q3, compared to 96 days in Q2. This is due to a combination of factors, including softening demand for certain consumer electronics products and increased competition in the market. We are implementing promotional campaigns and new product launches to stimulate demand and clear excess inventory. We are confident that our strategic initiatives will continue to drive improvements in inventory management and DOI in the coming quarters. The next target is to reduce DOI below 80 days and to improve the overall inventory turnover to above 4.5 times per year by the end of fiscal year 2024.

UMC experienced a foundry operating loss of 4.6% in Q1 2019. This represents a considerable decrease compared to Q4 2018, where UMC reported a positive operating margin of 2.8%. This translates to a QoQ decline of approximately 7.4 percentage points. This decline was primarily driven by seasonal weakness and inventory correction, lower ASPs, increased R&D spending, and Taiwan Dollar appreciation. Compared to Q1 2018, where UMC reported an operating margin of approximately 5.1%, the Q1 2019 performance represents a significant deterioration. This YoY decline of roughly 9.7 percentage points reflects the broader challenges facing the foundry industry, and UMC in particular. The key factors contributing to this YoY decline are oversupply and pricing pressure, shifting customer demand, impact of trade tensions, and increased depreciation expense. During the Q4 2018 earnings call, UMC provided guidance for Q1 2019, projecting an operating margin in the range of 0% to 2%. The actual reported operating margin of -4.6% fell significantly short of this guidance. This variance can be attributed to several factors, including underestimation of inventory correction, more aggressive pricing competition, delayed ramp-up of 22nm ULP, and unforeseen currency fluctuations.

Now to Dr. Li, who will cover operational and product updates.

Dr. Jian Li, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, Mr. Chen.

Let’s revisit the overall wafer ASP comments from an innovation standpoint:
We launched the StellarCore X5 processor, built on our advanced 5nm node, which contributed to a 12% ASP increase for 5nm in Q2. This is due to several factors: Firstly, this is the leading edge node, therefore more expensive. Secondly, the designs are incredibly intricate, demanding the tightest tolerances and advanced manufacturing techniques. And finally, our clients are demanding very specific specs for these wafers and are willing to pay a premium for them.

We’ve made strong headway with enhanced resource management, and expect meaningful results by the end of Q3 2019. We are investing in advanced resource management tools and processes to optimize project staffing and ensure that our consultants are effectively matched with projects that align with their skills and experience. This includes implementing an AI-powered resource allocation platform that will improve project forecasting accuracy and streamline resource deployment. We expect the new system to be fully operational by the end of Q3 2019.

Let’s move to Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
On the days of inventory, could you expand on the strategic initiatives being taken in the automotive sector to address the elevated DOI?

Mr. Chen:
Absolutely. We believe we have identified some key areas for improvement in the automotive segment. We have begun implementing a "digital twin" of our automotive supply chain, allowing us to simulate various disruption scenarios and identify potential bottlenecks. This initiative is expected to provide better visibility into our supply chain and enable more proactive inventory management. We are also exploring vendor-managed inventory (VMI) programs with select suppliers to reduce our on-hand inventory of key components. These initiatives should lead to a significant reduction in automotive DOI in the coming quarters.

Analyst 2:
Regarding the utilization rate, what's the scale and outlook?

Dr. Li:
We’re seeing momentum with our consulting services, especially in cybersecurity, driven by a 20% increase in our deal pipeline for cybersecurity-related projects. Our Q1 2019 utilization rate landed at 83%. While this demonstrates continued demand for our services, it represents a decrease from the 88% achieved in Q4 2018 and a more significant drop from the 94% reported in Q1 2018. Looking ahead to Q2 2019, our current guidance projects a utilization rate in the mid-80 percentage range. Beyond Q2, we are implementing several strategic initiatives to drive long-term utilization rate improvement.

Closing

Dr. Evelyn Reed:
Thank you all for joining. We’re proud of our progress and excited for what’s ahead.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes the call. You may now disconnect.
